pure-announcement.rationale: It is a consultancy argument piece, not a product launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: No existing concept covers the pilots-don't-scale-without-platform-architecture thesis or AgentOps; its sibling (the three-layers piece) is still in staging, not in the corpus.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The headline numbers are attributed to Bain's published AI readiness survey, so the empirical core is checkable even though the 'weeks, not months' payoff claim is not.

durability.rationale: Its load-bearing evidence is 2026 survey percentages (80% met expectations, 23% measurable value) — exactly the pass-rate/adoption-stat material that is stale in twelve months — while the durable kernel (AgentOps extending MLOps/LLMOps) gets only a passing definition.

actionability.rationale: It is executive case-making that explicitly defers the 'what to build' to later posts in the series, leaving a reader with an exhortation to invest but no mechanism, trade-off or step to act on.

atomicity.rationale: Everything serves one statable thesis — pilots stall because request-response architectures cannot support multi-turn agentic workflows — with the stats and benefits list as support.
